title: Extended Cech completion core reflector clauses
statement: For a small ringed site (C,J,O), a finite type ideal module I with monomorphism ι, and an augmented complex K ⟶ O[0] satisfying HasLocalExtendedCechDescription O I ι K ε, the internal-Hom completion functor has locally derived I-complete values and postcomposition with each canonical unit is bijective into every locally derived I-complete target.

source.place: Tags 099B and 099F, completeness and universal mapping clauses of proposition-derived-completion

proof.text: Reconstruct naturality of the specified augmentation-induced unit from naturality of evaluation at one and fully faithful whiskering by Q. This repeats the independent calculation from the parent as a private proved helper, since importing that parent would create a cycle. For any exact slice restriction and isomorphism of augmented derived objects, use the RHom restriction comparison and normalize its ring-object component to obtain a natural comparison preserving the actual unit.

Take a finite ideal-generating cover. The local extended Cech description gives augmented derived isomorphisms on its slices. The independent finite-Cech unit-idempotence theorem says both G.map(eta) and eta_G are invertible there. Naturality of the normalized completion comparison transfers these two assertions to the restriction of F.map(eta) and eta_F for the global model. Exact restriction commutes with cohomology; the ordinary sheaf isomorphism criterion on a cover therefore descends both isomorphisms.
Apply the single-object completeness/unit criterion to F(E). Its unit is invertible by the preceding step, hence the completion value is locally derived complete.

For a complete target L, the same criterion makes eta_L invertible. Given f:E→L, the morphism F.map(f) followed by inverse eta_L extends f, by naturality. If eta_E followed by g and by h agree, apply F and cancel the invertible F.map(eta_E); then cancel eta_L using naturality to deduce g=h. This proves the displayed bijection without another geometric hypothesis.

lean.statement: theorem ringedExtendedCech_reflector_core {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O))] [∀ U : C, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u} ((sheafCompose (J.over U) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj (O.over U)))] (I : ringedSiteModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O)) (ι : I ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O)) [Mono ι] [I.IsFiniteType] (K : ringedSiteComplex O) (ε : K ⟶ ringedSiteRingComplex O) (hK : HasLocalExtendedCechDescription O I ι K ε) : (∀ E : ringedSiteDerived O, IsLocallyDerivedRingedIdealComplete O I ι ((ringedCechCompletionFunctor O K).obj E)) ∧ (∀ (E L : ringedSiteDerived O), IsLocallyDerivedRingedIdealComplete O I ι L → Function.Bijective (fun h : (ringedCechCompletionFunctor O K).obj E ⟶ L ↦ ringedCechCompletionUnit O K ε E ≫ h))
